mbm-0493.clue: My mug keeps its elbow on the table.
mbm-0493.quote: I pulled one handle too far before the clay dried. It rests on the table like an elbow. Dad uses that mug when he wants to sit and talk for a while.

mbm-0494.clue: The bails only come out at low tide.
mbm-0494.quote: I found two pieces of driftwood that balance on our beach stumps. My little cousin keeps them wrapped in a handkerchief like silverware. He unrolls them and declares the sand officially open.

mbm-0495.clue: Friday television has its own weather.
mbm-0495.quote: I stretch a blue sheet over the sofa for submarine shows. My cousins sit underneath in pajamas. When it starts to rain on screen, I tap the sheet with my fingertips till everybody ducks.

mbm-0496.clue: The map on my radio desk has a sewing needle in it.
mbm-0496.quote: Each station I reach gets a loop of thread round a pin. Last month two operators who'd never met turned out to live on the same street. I tied their threads together with the smallest knot I could manage.

mbm-0497.clue: My program serves the soup first.
mbm-0497.quote: I wrote a kitchen timer for our home computer. Instead of ringing it draws a little bowl filling with steam. When the real soup and the pixel soup are ready together, my brother sets a place for the machine.

mbm-0498.clue: I borrowed a book through a hedge.
mbm-0498.quote: My neighbor used to leave novels on the low wall between our gardens. One wet spring I made a roof from an old baking tray. Now the smallest lending library I know stays dry in a downpour.

mbm-0499.clue: My oldest buckle has two sunsets in it.
mbm-0499.quote: I polished one half of a brass buckle and left the other half dark. Set it on my leather workbench at dusk and the bright half holds the window while the dark half holds the room.

mbm-0500.clue: This patch came out of a borrowed uniform.
mbm-0500.quote: I made a quilt from my family's old jobs. A nurse gave me blue cotton, a painter gave me gray. Dad's strip is from the striped tie he wore the day he finally got his own desk.

mbm-0501.clue: My oldest lesson fits between two floorboards.
mbm-0501.quote: When I rushed a turn my heel landed on a squeaky seam. I practiced till the seam stayed quiet. Years later I still start my forms on that spot to see how gently I can arrive.

mbm-0502.clue: My first game has a shop that never closes.
mbm-0502.quote: I wrote a tiny game about our corner grocer and forgot to give the store a closing time. Mum played at midnight and bought a pixel orange. We left the light on in that little shop forever.

mbm-0503.clue: I count the blue flags on the way back.
mbm-0503.quote: On backstroke I once drifted so far that the flags looked like a string of kites. My coach handed me a little paper kite after I swam a straight length. It hangs above my swim bag.

mbm-0504.clue: The best part of my trophy melted on the way home.
mbm-0504.quote: The fair served our prize sundaes in little gold cups. Mine started melting on the bus, so I shared it with my brother at the next stop. He still claims half the title.

mbm-0505.clue: I can tell which chapter needed the train whistle.
mbm-0505.quote: I draft stories beside the tracks. Whenever the whistle drowns out my sentence I draw a long line on the page. In my last story that line became the road the sisters finally took home.

mbm-0506.clue: My baduk teacher kept one stone warm.
mbm-0506.quote: Grandpa hid a white stone in his palm while I studied the board. When I found the move he opened his hand. I can still remember the warmth of the stone he passed me.

mbm-0507.clue: The lid plays our opening note.
mbm-0507.quote: I turn the wooden lid of our baduk bowl over before we start. My cousin drops one black stone into it; the little knock means the talking is over. After the game we let the bowl ring twice.

mbm-0508.clue: The kite quilt has a pocket for the wind.
mbm-0508.quote: I stitched a small open flap under one cloth kite. When the quilt hangs on the line the wind slips in and lifts that kite above the others. My niece calls it the one that got away.

mbm-0509.clue: I visit the big hall for a very small reflection.
mbm-0509.quote: The polished foot of a bronze horse reflects the museum's glass ceiling. I sit on the floor and draw that little ceiling, pane by pane. I still haven't drawn the rest of the horse.

mbm-0510.clue: My second controller is for the mechanic.
mbm-0510.quote: My racing game has one driver, but my little brother takes the unplugged controller to work the imaginary pit crew. I have never had four tires changed with more button presses.

mbm-0511.clue: My summer chair leaves paw prints.
mbm-0511.quote: I put cloth pads on the feet so my beach chair wouldn't scrape the sunny patio. My sister cut them in paw shapes. After a shower the chair walks four neat wet paws across the stone.

mbm-0512.clue: I made a hat for a jar of jam.
mbm-0512.quote: My kitchen shelf was chilly enough to set the honey, so I crocheted little caps for my jars. Gran picked the strawberry cap for herself and asked for earflaps before remembering her head was bigger.

mbm-0513.clue: The waltz is longer in the hallway.
mbm-0513.quote: I practiced alone until my sister opened both doors at once and made the hallway into a ballroom. We had space for exactly three more steps. I still call them the borrowed three.

mbm-0514.clue: I came home with a seat for the bread.
mbm-0514.quote: I promised my gran I'd bring her sourdough across the lake without squashing it. I strapped a bread tin in front of my kayak and tucked the loaf inside. When I arrived she lifted the lid like a tiny oven door. The crust crackled when she cut it.

mbm-0515.clue: I paint a little rain under every roof.
mbm-0515.quote: My father was a roofer. When I paint houses he stretches out a finger and shows me where runoff would fall. I put one fine silver stroke there, even if it's a sunny day.

mbm-0516.clue: Our cricket boundary travels on two feet.
mbm-0516.quote: We marked the beach boundary with my brother's sandals. Halfway through the match he got hungry, put them on and wandered off for chips. We had to call the smallest ground in history.

mbm-0517.clue: My win screen is a sheet of notebook paper.
mbm-0517.quote: When our old game ended it went straight back to the start. My friend drew a ridiculous victory parade and held it in front of the TV whenever I won. That piece of paper is still my favorite level.
